Resolves #21869

Learning chooses its deck from the browser query string before it loads the tree. Valid campaign parameters could throw in the former JSON-based parser and leave the deck unset. The parser now uses `URLSearchParams` and preserves the last value for repeated keys.

Evidence: L2 focused unit tests. PR scope is the Portal parser and its existing spec.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 1 | The regression fails against the old parser with `SyntaxError`. The corrected parser reads a bare key, embedded equals signs, encoded delimiters and quotes, and a space encoded as `+`. With no `deck` key, the Learn controller uses its existing `learnneo` fallback. |
| 2 | The spec verifies last-value selection for a repeated explicit deck and an empty object for null, empty and bare-question-mark queries. |
| 3 | The Portal utility and Learn route helpers passed all 17 focused tests. |

## Deltas from ticket

None.

`npm run test-unit -- --workers=1 --reporter=dot test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/Util.spec.mjs test/playwright/unit/apps/portal/LearnRoutes.spec.mjs` → 17/17 passed. Commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed. `agent-preflight` is hosted outside the Engine repo.

Its only consumer is `apps/portal/view/learn/MainContainerController.mjs:39`, inside a `.then`, so a throw there never reaches `setState` and the tree never loads. `Object.fromEntries(new URLSearchParams(searchString ?? ''))` drops the leading `?` by the platform's rule, keeps the last of repeated keys and answers `{}` for null, an empty string and a bare `?`; the three new tests pin each of those in the existing `Util.spec.mjs`.
